svg.title: The scary numbers ask for everything at once
svg.desc: IFScale, July 2025: Up to 500 keywords, all required in one business report. The best model reached 68% at 500, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet 52.7%. Every instruction applies to the same piece of writing. Prompt Design at Scale, July 2026: 10 to 160 rules on one short essay, marked by code. Getting all of them right fell to almost zero by 80 rules for every model. Claude Sonnet 5 went from 93.8% at 10 rules to 23.8% at 40. Instruction Stacking Collapse, July 2026: Up to 20 rules stacked on one reply. Claude Sonnet 4.6 fell from 96.4% to 60.4%, and much of the fall came from rules that clash with each other. Anthropic's Claude Code docs: Asks for fewer than 200 lines per CLAUDE.md, saying longer files use up context and get followed less closely. The page doesn't say by how much, and it is written for a coding agent in long sessions. None of these tested a Claude 5.5 model, and none measured a long list where only a few rules apply.
svg.text: The scary numbers ask for everything at once
Each study piles many rules onto a single piece of writing. A team's
rulebook mostly holds rules that don't apply to the reply in hand.

52.7%. Every instruction applies to the same piece of

Anthropic's Claude Code
docs
Asks for fewer than 200 lines per CLAUDE.md, saying
longer files use up context and get followed less
closely. The page doesn't say by how much, and it is
written for a coding agent in long sessions.
None of these tested a Claude 5.5 model, and none measured a long list where only a
few rules apply.
